condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from

a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: Sumatriptan, which shares the indole-ethylamine core with the query, has human oral bioavailability of 14–15%, below the 20% threshold.
DMT, also a tryptamine, has estimated absolute oral bioavailability of about 10–15% in ayahuasca, below the threshold.
Eluxadoline, a zwitterionic poorly permeable molecule, has F of about 1%, consistent with the query's very low neutral fraction and poor passive-permeability liability.

Additional low-F contexts (propafenone under rifampin, epanolol with food, tetracycline, agomelatine) are less directly transferable because of condition or structural differences, but they do not contradict the low direction.

High-F contexts (tadalafil, ketanserin, fluvastatin) are structurally dissimilar or borderline; tadalafil records are internally inconsistent (36% vs ~80%), so they do not outweigh the low-F analog evidence.

evidence_gaps: No direct oral bioavailability measurement exists for the query molecule itself.
The most transferable low-F analogs (sumatriptan, DMT) lack the hydroxamic acid and zwitterionic features of the query, so their metabolic and transport behavior may differ.
No query-specific permeability, first-pass metabolism, or transporter data are available.
Condition-specific low-F records (rifampin induction, fed state) are not directly applicable to the query's no-condition state.
High-F contexts are structurally dissimilar, leaving their relevance uncertain.

This is progressive assay-transfer reasoning. The target is the task endpoint,

sampling context together.

formulation, dose, study design, consistency, limitations, or why an L1 outcome

oral-bioavailability outcome.

votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
